newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse amends trading rules from Sept 9.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse amends trading rules from Sept 9.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday that its amended trading rules, approved by the State Securities and Exchange Supervision (AETF) on September 4, will take effect on Monday.
One main change will be that spot trading may be implemented only via computers and not via open outcry, the BSE said in a statement.
Currently 58 securities, including less actively traded shares and notes of investment funds, are traded via open outcry of the around 170 securities which are traded on the bourse, it said.
These 58 securities accounted for only 1.92 percent of total bourse turnover and for around nine percent of number of deals in 1995, it added.

Another change will be that all shares will be traded at the same time, dropping the current system in which the automatically traded shares were divided into three groups with trading running for around 30 minutes for each group.
Also, the bourse will abolish the difference between the limit price and the so-called book price, cutting down chances for speculation.
"If the limit and the book prices are the same this will presumably boost the market's transparency and help more balanced prices," it said.
